description.narrative: The proposed project will support inclusive, resilient, and sustainable urban infrastructure and services in four secondary cities (Djizzak, Havast, Khiva, and Yangiyer) experiencing low livability and lagging growth exacerbated by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. It will demonstrate integrated and innovative solutions, and strengthen institutional capacity for "building back better". These measures will (i) enhance livability for residents and visitors, including persons with disabilities; (ii) support green and resilient economic recovery targeting women; (iii) accelerate digital transformation, particularly in the tourism and water sectors; and (iv) increase the quality, coverage, efficiency, and reliability of urban services. The project supports the government's national development strategy, 2022-2026, which aims to accelerate growth and reduce poverty through improved urbanization and balanced regional development.

description.narrative: Access to inclusive, resilient, and sustainable urban services in secondary cities enhanced.

At least 142,068 people in Khiva, Havast, and Djizzak benefit from access to new or improved public parks and open green spaces with EWCD-friendly features to cope with more extreme heat waves. Progress/Status: Havast (UR01) package awarded 3 November 2023. Physical progress as of 31 December 2025 is 79%. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports, project completion report, asset owner annual reports Actual value:

100% household coverage of solid waste collection and environmentally sustainable SWM services benefiting at least 341,400 people in the four project cities. Progress/Status: Per agreement in the timebound action plan in the Mission Aide Memoire from the October 2025 review mission, the EA was meant to submit by 15 December the plan for SWM packages. On November 28th the ADB held a meeting between the MOEF and the Circular Economy Agency, to discuss in detail Government of Uzbekistan's SWM strategy and align the existing requests for support with the project objectives. In January 2026 the ADB received through MOEF information provided by the Circular Economy Agency which partially addresses the rationale for procurement of EVs, however the technical justification and supporting studies has yet to be provided. The MOEF had conducted a site visit and provided photographic evidence (overflowing trashcans, mismanaged collection points) which support the need to continue with the originally planned project outputs. The MOEF expressed the need to continue with the original scope of the project and have proposed brining the issue to the National Committee Management. . Data Source: PIU quarterly reports, project completion report, asset owner annual reports Actual value:

At least 173,636 people in Djizzak benefit from sustainable and resilient potable piped water supply with at least 8 hours continuous service/day and an average of 113 lpcd. Progress/Status: Djizzak water supply package (WS01) awarded in November 2023. As of 31 December 2025, contractor has installed 12.2km of pipes. Physical progress is 47% and behind schedule. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports, project completion report, asset owner annual reports Baseline value: 4 hours
